competitive_landscape: The water today is run by chartered diesel speedboats for the gateway transfer and inter-island day-trips, with resorts handling their own boats; access is improving via the new Maratua airstrip but the on-water last mile remains a fragmented, road-plus-speedboat affair. For a destination with assets this rare, the transfer layer is basic, loud, and rough on guests and reefs alike. A clean, fast, quiet foiling network closes that gap — and the established resort cluster and growing liveaboard interest show the demand is already there.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The all-electric core: the mainland shuttle Tanjung Redeb↔Derawan ~25 nm and the intra-archipelago Derawan–Maratua–Kakaban–Sangalaki mesh (~5–40 nm), with Half-Foil/Shallow-Mode for the reef-dense Marine Park geometry and low-wake, quiet-mode operation around turtle and manta sites. Tarakan↔Derawan ~50 nm sits at the upper edge of all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The East Kalimantan line-hauls: Balikpapan↔Derawan and IKN Nusantara↔Derawan ~340 nm, Samarinda ~290 nm, Maratua↔Tarakan ~85 nm, and the Talisayan whale-shark run along the Berau coast. Hybrid range with no charging dependency suits island microgrids; Indonesia's second-largest refinery at Balikpapan plus Pertamina depots at Tarakan and Tanjung Redeb give the deepest diesel-refuel supply chain of any eastern-Indonesia cluster.

precedents.what: $100M, ~100-vessel phased electric-foiling network with JIH Global
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a dispersed dive-and-charter archipelago can adopt a clean-foiling network at scale — directly relevant to Derawan's resort cluster and gateway corridors.

regulatory_note: Co-firing conservation channels — KKP's Berau Marine Park (2005) plus KLHK/BB-KSDA's Sangalaki and Kakaban marine tourism parks — alongside Kemenhub/DGST + BKI on transport. Turtle-nesting light restrictions and the in-lake no-motor protocol at Kakaban make a zero-emission, low-wake, quiet-mode fleet a clean fit. The IKN Nusantara new-capital ferry-terminal build is a rare greenfield opportunity to design clean-marine charging and refuel architecture in from the start.
seasonality: Aligned (not inverted): the dry, calm season Apr–Oct is the peak — best visibility, the Talisayan whale-shark aggregation and Sangalaki mantas all coincide with the smoothest seas. The NE monsoon (Nov–Mar) brings mild rain and some Sulawesi Sea swell but no closure, and the area sits outside the NW-Pacific typhoon track — a structural reliability advantage. Foiling smooths the semi-exposed Tarakan–Berau strait and the Makassar Strait throughflow on the mainland line-hauls.
signature_routes: Tanjung Redeb / Berau ↔ Derawan (gateway last-mile) — Pioneer II
Derawan ↔ Maratua ↔ Kakaban ↔ Sangalaki (intra-archipelago dive mesh) — Pioneer II
IKN Nusantara / Balikpapan ↔ Derawan (new-capital corridor) — Quanta-LR
summary: The Derawan Archipelago off NE Borneo is a Coral Triangle gem: Kakaban's stingless jellyfish lake (one of only two on earth), Sangalaki's manta cleaning stations and Indonesia's largest green-turtle nesting site, and the Talisayan whale-shark aggregation. Guests fly into Berau (or the new Maratua airstrip), then transfer by road and diesel speedboat to a cluster of mid-tier dive resorts. The islands sit a tidy 5–40 nm apart — ideal all-electric range — while the East Kalimantan mainland gateways, including Indonesia's new capital at IKN Nusantara, are a clean Quanta-LR line-haul away.
tagline: Borneo's dive archipelago — stingless jellyfish lakes and manta cleaning stations, reached by road transfer and diesel speedboat.

use_cases.body: A smooth, quiet all-electric circuit between Derawan, Maratua, Kakaban and Sangalaki — replacing diesel speedboats with Half-Foil/Shallow-Mode reef-pass handling and low-wake, quiet-mode operation around the turtle-nesting beaches and manta stations.
